primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy due to JC polyomavirus
mechanism: JC polyomavirus usually persists latently but can reactivate during severe cellular immunosuppression. In the CNS it productively infects and lyses oligodendrocytes, the myelin-forming cells of the central nervous system, producing multifocal areas of white-matter demyelination with relatively spared axons.
vignette: A 41-year-old man with untreated HIV infection and a CD4 count of 48/mm3 develops 6 weeks of progressive clumsiness of the right hand, difficulty finding words, and loss of vision in the right visual field. He has no fever or headache. Brain MRI shows several asymmetric hyperintense lesions in the subcortical white matter without substantial mass effect. Cerebrospinal fluid PCR detects JC polyomavirus DNA.
lead: Lytic infection of which of the following cell types is primarily responsible for this patient's neurologic disease?
distractor_notes: Schwann cells form myelin in the peripheral nervous system, whereas PML is a central white-matter demyelinating disease.
Anterior horn motor neurons are targeted in disorders such as poliomyelitis; their destruction causes lower-motor-neuron weakness rather than multifocal cerebral white-matter lesions.
Microglia are resident CNS macrophage-lineage cells and participate in inflammatory responses but are not the principal myelin-forming cell lysed in PML.
Cerebral endothelial injury can disrupt the blood-brain barrier in vascular/inflammatory disorders but does not explain JC-virus-mediated demyelination.
key_expl: Progressive focal neurologic deficits in a severely immunocompromised patient, multifocal white-matter lesions with little mass effect, and JC-virus DNA in CSF identify PML. JC virus undergoes productive lytic infection in oligodendrocytes, destroying the cells responsible for CNS myelin and causing multifocal demyelination.
objective: Recognize PML in severe cellular immunosuppression and link JC polyomavirus to lytic destruction of CNS oligodendrocytes and multifocal demyelination.
